title: fix(plugin-view): say what handleRowClick does with a modifier click (objectui#9806)
body:
**Part of #9806** — this lands the comment half only. The behaviour half survives the merge and is named below, so this PR deliberately does not carry a closing keyword. The card itself states the two are separable and that a taker may do only the second.

## 1. Which of the two is wrong — settled by reading, not inherited

Read at `origin/main` `6778809f5`, 2026-09-18T13:12Z. **The COMMENT is wrong. The code is doing what three landed cards asked it to do.**

`packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts`, inside `handleClick` — the early return stands AHEAD of the modifier branch:

```
      if (onRowClick) {
        onRowClick(record, event);
        return;
      }

      // Modifier / middle-click -> always open in a new browser tab as a full
      // page. ...
      const isModifierClick = !!(
        event && (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.button === 1)
      );
```

`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` hands its callback down at both sites, neither of them gated on a host handler:

```
        onRowClick: handleRowClick,        // the renderListView host slot
        onRowClick={handleRowClick}        // the default ObjectGrid branch
```

and each receiver forwards that prop straight into the hook as its `onRowClick` — `ObjectGrid` and `ListView` both end their `useNavigationOverlay({ ... })` call with a bare `onRowClick,`.

⇒ there is no arm in which the hook's modifier branch runs for this component. The sentence "is the hook's own decision, taken before this callback runs" describes a delegation that does not happen.

⛔ **And the early return is NOT the defect.** It is the whole point of objectui#9357 / objectui#9360 / objectui#9462: a host that supplies a handler must receive the payload and decide for itself. Removing it would take that decision away from every host that already has one. So option (2) — "the code is wrong" — is refused on the reading, not deferred for convenience: a modifier branch that outranked a host handler would be a different and worse contract. What is left is a behaviour QUESTION (should this component implement the convention itself?), which is a change on a published component and is not settled here.

## 2. The user-visible consequence today, and how it was determined

Determined by DRIVING it, not by reasoning about it — the pin this PR adds renders the real component, fires the clicks and reads the destination. Measured:

- With no host `onRowClick` and no authored `navigation`: a plain click and a ⌘-click both reach `onNavigate(recordId, 'view')`. **It navigates in place. No browser tab is opened.**
- Ctrl-click and middle-click land identically — all three spellings of the payload.
- The payload still ARRIVES at `handleRowClick` (objectui#9462's repair is intact and pinned here). It is received and not read.

⇒ the honest phrasing of the user-visible half is not "a new tab fails to open" but **"a modifier click on an ObjectView row is indistinguishable from a plain click"**. Whatever the authored navigation mode does for an ordinary click is what a modifier click gets; where that mode is `new_window`, every click opens a tab and the modifier is still not what caused it.

⚠️ **A second fact, measured while building the probe and NOT in the card.** The `gridSchema` that `ObjectView` builds carries neither `navigation` nor `onNavigate`. So even with the early return deleted, the hook's modifier branch on this path would find no `onNavigate` and no `navigation`, fall through, and do nothing. **A future behaviour card cannot be "delete the early return" — it also has to give the grid a navigation destination.** This is reported, not acted on.

## 3. The instrument — the half this seat called the more valuable one

A rewritten sentence with no instrument is the same defect deferred, so the comment now CITES a pin by name and the pin reads that citation back out of the file. `packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.modifierClickInPlace-9806.test.tsx`, 11 cases:

- **SUBJECT** — the real `ObjectView` default branch, no host handler: plain click and modifier click are asserted INDISTINGUISHABLE. That equivalence is exactly what the amended comment claims.
- **LIVENESS CONTROL** — a bare `ObjectGrid` with no `onRowClick`: its two clicks DIVERGE (`'view'` vs `'new_window'`). Without it, a probe that never delivered `metaKey` would produce the subject's green.
- **ISOLATION CONTROL** — the SAME `ObjectGrid` call with one prop added, an unconditional `onRowClick`. This is the one-variable pair, and it is what attributes the subject's equivalence to the early return rather than to the composition. ⚠️ The liveness control does NOT vary one thing against the subject and the file says so; claiming it did would have been this card's own defect.
- **SOURCE-TEXT** — comments stripped, because the subject file documents the construct being asserted on. The strip is controlled in both directions (`event.metaKey` present raw, absent stripped), and the presence leg on the hook is keyed on the READ spelling, with `metaKey?: boolean` pinned beside it so a member DECLARATION can never be mistaken for a read.
- **HANDSHAKE** — the comment must name this file, and the pin derives its own name from `import.meta.url` rather than typing it, so a rename reds too.

⚠️ Measured and recorded rather than assumed: the `handleRowClick` BODY case does **not** depend on the strip — its slice starts at the callback, so the comment above it is already outside the text read, and disabling the stripper leaves that case green. The strip is kept there for a comment moved INSIDE the callback later; the case that re-derives the strip's liveness is the whole-file one.

## 4. Ablations — every one predicted before it ran

Mutation landed proven by blob hash, restore proven by hash equality AND an empty `git diff HEAD`, trap on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths.

| # | mutation | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | revert `ObjectView.tsx` to `6778809f5` (put the FALSE comment back) | handshake + raw-bytes stripper control RED; all behavioural GREEN | **2 failed / 9 passed — exactly those two** |
| B | gate `handleClick`'s early return on the click not being a modifier click | subject modifier cases, ordering case, isolation control RED; plain click + liveness control GREEN | **4 failed / 7 passed — exactly those four** |
| C | make the hand-down conditional (`onRowClick ? handleRowClick : undefined`) | the three subject cases RED, nothing observed | **3 failed / 8 passed** |
| D | make the comment stripper the identity function | only the whole-file stripper case RED | **1 failed / 10 passed** |

⭐ **Reported because it is the honest result, not hidden:** in ablation A every BEHAVIOURAL case stayed GREEN. It has to — this PR changes no behaviour. The legs that were red before this change are the handshake and the raw-bytes control, and those are what make the delivered pin one that would have been red before it.

The sweep set was derived, not guessed: every test that READS either changed file at runtime (`readFileSync` / `sourceOf`), with a control file that reads none — `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.relayRungCensus-7559.test.ts`, `packages/react/src/hooks/__tests__/` (both arity pins), six `packages/types/src/__tests__/` readers, `examples/schema-catalog`, three `scripts/__tests__/` files, the objectui#9462 behavioural pin, and the whole of `packages/plugin-view`.

**Declared narrowing:** `check:doc-examples` is build-gated on every package's `dist` and is left to CI. Its inputs from this file are byte-unmoved — it reads JSDoc `@example` on exported declarations, this diff adds and removes none, and the count in `ObjectView.tsx` is 3 before and 3 after, matching its three keyed entries.

## 6. Pending changeset sweep

Swept the pending `.changeset/` directory for any body this diff makes false. The one entry on this subject is `9462-row-click-modifier-payload-forward.md` (package-declaring frontmatter, so it does publish a CHANGELOG line). It is **not** falsified: every claim in it is scoped to a host that supplies a handler — "reaches a host handler", "a host wiring a modifier-click handler ... always read `undefined`" — which is exactly the boundary this card sits outside of. No edit made to it.

A whole-tree sweep for the removed sentence found it in this one file and nowhere else. ⚠️ That took three attempts: the first two probes returned a confident zero because the sentence is line-wrapped and each line carries a `//` prefix. The published form strips comment markers and collapses newlines, and it was re-run in that exact form with a control that fires.

## Acceptance notes

- **Noted, not filed — the hook's own neighbouring comment.** `useNavigationOverlay.ts` says the early return forwards the payload "so parent handlers (e.g. ObjectView) can still implement Cmd/Ctrl/middle-click". That is a capability claim and it is true; `ObjectView` simply does not take it up. It is adjacent to this card's defect class without being an instance, so it is left alone rather than edited on the way past. Successor: the behaviour card, if one is opened.
- **The `gridSchema` navigation gap** in section 2 is the substantive finding for whoever takes the behaviour half.
- Not marked ready, no auto-merge, not merged — the seat lands it.
